title: Don Ewell's piano, Bunk's praise, and unrecorded tunes
summary: Don Ewell's Jelly Roll style and four-beat left hand, Bunk calling him his number one pianist, and an unrecorded tune the band played.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. And who is Don Ewell?

Well, he's a piano player from Baltimore, uh, plays many, well, he has a way, uh, a style which, uh, uh, uses many of the stylisms, uh, uh, from the jazz tradition. And, and, uh, at that particular time, uh, he was very much on a jelly kick, and, and, uh, we used to stand behind the piano when he was playing with Bunk and, and just listen to the piano. He was playing beautiful jelly roll style piano.
And, uh, uh, well, specifically in the ensemble, what kind of thing would he be doing?

Well, he, uh, uh, basically was playing, uh, uh, a four beats to the bar, uh, things, uh, generally, uh, uh, I guess the same kind of part that, that, uh, Alton Purnell played, which is, uh, uh, uh, an octaves left hand playing, uh, almost a boogie woogie type figure, but just four beats to the bar, uh, going up and down a chord, uh, in the left hand. And, uh, in the left hand, and, and the right hand chordings around the middle of the piano along with it, and sometimes breaking up the rhythm, but the, the basic thing was this, uh, four beats to the bar, uh, identical, musically identical, uh, figures on all four beats, instead of being a two beat type thing, an umpah. Instead of being an umpah, he was a, uh, uh, studied figure.
And, uh, uh, for his solos, he would play a stride style or a jolly roll style.
Do you remember any outstanding nights, uh, outstanding solos that really stick in your mind?
I can't remember the solos, uh, or, or nor the nights. I, I mean, I can just remember being dazzled, uh, many times.
Yeah, but I mean, an old thing like, you don't remember anybody particularly complimenting Don on something, or Bunk, or Bunk's attitude towards Don, or something like that?

Well, I remember that Bunk was very pleased with Don's playing, and, and used to get up from his seat and walk over to the piano and play a chorus with, with the piano, and just kind of get together with him, you know, so they could hear each other better, and, and, uh, uh, uh, uh, Bunk always had the best things to say about Don's playing. I know he always wanted to use them when he could. He called him his number one piano player.
Do you remember any favorite tunes that weren't recorded?

Uh, there was one that they used to play with, where they played with Don in the band that was never recorded, but I'm not sure. I think it was all alone on the telephone. I'm trying to piece it together now afterwards, uh, but it had a theme in it, uh, there's no place like home theme, and, and, and somewhere stuck in the middle of the tune. And, uh, I think it was some Irving Berlin thing, but it was real pretty. They, they really did it well. And, uh, outside of that, and Honeysuckle, and, uh, Mylenberg Joyce, I don't know if they ever recorded that or not. Did they record that, the punk record, Mylenberg?
Mylenberg, but not Honeysuckle, I don't know.
